sentences.text: Ornithosuchus was traditionally estimated to be about 4 meters long, but recent studies have revised this maximum length to 2.2 meters.
The animal was first described by Newton in 1894.

Ornithosuchus belongs to the unranked order Crurotarsi and is classified within the family Ornithosuchidae, which included geographically widespread, facultatively bipedal carnivores in the Late Triassic.
Only one species, O. woodwardi, is currently recognized for Ornithosuchus, while O. taylori is considered a synonym, though the type species is O. longidens, originally named Dasygnathus longidens.
Fossils of Ornithosuchus date to the Late Triassic period, when it lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
